key_insight: World from Motion turns monocular video into freely renderable dynamic 3D Gaussian scenes by using motion-aware, pixel-aligned conditioning to repair artifacts and complete missing geometry. In simple terms, it learns a better 3D world model from one camera view by leveraging motion and multi-view-style supervision.
problem_solved: The paper tackles the challenge of reconstructing high-quality, dynamic 3D scenes from only a monocular video, where naive methods often produce rendering artifacts, holes, and incomplete motion-aware geometry.
method: Condition a video generation model on dense, pixel-aligned renderings that encode appearance, geometry, and 3D scene motion.
Use both input and target camera trajectories to guide the model in correcting artifacts and hallucinating missing regions.
Train on a constructed dataset of aligned multiview video pairs and dynamic 3D Gaussian representations to improve reconstruction quality.
impact: This enables more realistic, freely navigable dynamic scene reconstruction from simple monocular footage, which is useful for robotics, AR/VR, digital twins, and content creation. For practitioners, it offers a practical path to better 3D video understanding without requiring expensive multi-camera capture.

paper_title: World from Motion: Generative Dynamic Gaussian Reconstruction from Monocular Video
paper_authors: Liyuan Zhu, Shengyu Huang, Amrita Mazumdar, Tianye Li, Zan Gojcic
